observations:
After reviewing the source text of LM2 Torah 12 in full, the four packages identified in the gap analysis (torah_12_packages.json) are sufficient to cover all bechina-connected concepts in this Torah. No independent domain of 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language was found that would require a fifth package.

The four packages cleanly cover the Torah's entire conceptual map:
  Package 1 (כָּבוֹד עֶלְיוֹן / מַאֲמָר סָתוּם / 'אַיֵּה') — the hidden transcendent domain
  Package 2 (כָּבוֹד / עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת / תְּמִימוּת) — the revealed structural domain
  Package 3 (קְלִפַּת נֹגַהּ / סְפֵקוֹת / עֵץ הַדַּעַת) — the evil/mixed obstructing domain
  Package 4 (תְּשׁוּבָה / עוֹלָה / עֵץ הַחַיִּים) — the return/rectification domain

Candidate concepts reviewed and their dispositions:

1. 'כְּרַךְ גָּדוֹל שֶׁל רוֹמִי' (the great city of Rome) — mentioned in line 20 as an example of a place where God is hidden. This is an illustrative example (nimshal) rather than a bechina-connected concept. It does not form a cluster; it is a single proof-text illustration of the 'mekkomot hamtunafim' theme. Absorbed into Package 3 as an example, not a separate node.

2. חָכְמָה וְשֵׂכֶל (wisdom and intellect) — mentioned in line 1 as the source of the wicked's errors. The Torah does not call this a bechina of anything; it is the starting-point problem, not a bechina-connected node. It represents the opposite of temimut but is only mentioned in the opening frame, not developed with bechina language.

3. 'יִרְאָה / יָרֵא שַׁבָּת' — mentioned in the editorial note (line 28) as a related topic (from a later Torah). The Rebbe himself notes 'שַׁיָּךְ גַּם כֵּן לְכָאן' but explains this is a matter for a different section. No bechina language connects it to this Torah's structure.

4. הַשְׁגָּחָה (divine providence) — similarly mentioned in line 29 as connected to this Torah through the Aggadah of the rooster's gaze. Again, the Rebbe notes 'שַׁיָּךְ גַּם כֵּן לָזֶה' but states 'לֹא זָכִינוּ לִשְׁמֹעַ בֵּאוּר כָּל זֶה' — we did not merit to hear the full explanation. Without that explanation, no bechina structure can be reliably extracted for hashgacha in this Torah.

5. שִׂמְחָה / בְּדִיחָא דַּעְתָּא (joy) — mentioned in the editorial note (line 26) as part of the cluster of related utterances. Again, this belongs to a different section and is only referenced as connected to this Torah through the same Aggadah. The Rebbe does not provide bechina language connecting it to the core packages.

Conclusion: The four packages derived from the source text are complete and self-contained. The Torah's argument is fully covered by the good/evil/good/good polarity structure: revealed kavod (good) → kelipat nogah/doubts (evil) → hidden kavod/ayeh (good) → teshuvah/ascent (good). No additional independent domain warrants a new package.
